glossary.note: Officialdom has formal laws, and the common people have their agreements for peace.

glossary.en: qin shou zhi tu - 'a company of beasts'
glossary.note: People who forget kindness and have no humanity.

pian15.background: This section quotes the words of Confucius in the Analects, Lu Ji's 'Rhapsody on Literature' (Wen fu) and a poem by Yu Liangshi, which shows how the book gathers lines from literati poetry and folk proverbs. Lines such as 'to forget kindness and betray rightness is to be a beast' reflect the traditional respect for teachers and rightness.

pian16.summary: This last section is mostly about urging study, accumulating virtue, thrift, contentment and keeping to one's lot, as in 'rather than pile up money, pile up virtue; rather than buy land, buy books', and closes with 'to the gentleman I would say: each should keep to himself'.
pian16.translation: I urge you not to fry vegetables in oil, but to leave the oil for your sons and grandsons to read by at night. In books there is a thousand bushels of grain; in books there is a face like jade. Do not blame Heaven and do not blame men; the five phases and the eight characters decide one's fate. Do not grumble at being poor; if you are poor, be cleanly poor. Do not envy others for being rich; if you are rich, be nobly rich. Others ride horses and I ride a donkey; thinking it over I am worse off, but when I turn and look, there is still the porter carrying loads. There are hungry people on the road, and leftover rice at home. Pile up virtue for your sons and grandsons; do people favours widely. When you do good, spirits respect you; when you do evil, Heaven punishes you. To pile up money and grain is not as good as to pile up virtue; to buy fields and land is not as good as to buy books. One day's spring work is worth ten days' grain; ten days' spring work is worth half a year's grain. The lazy have nothing to eat; the diligent and thrifty have full granaries. People are close but wealth is not close, so keep gain clearly separate. Of ten parts of cleverness use seven, always leaving three for your sons and grandsons; if you use all ten, it is far from your descendants and close to yourself. The noble person is glad to be a noble person; the petty man is a petty man to no purpose. Those who love learning, even the child of a commoner may become a minister; those who do not, even the child of a minister may become a commoner. The one who begrudges money should not teach his son; the one who shields his own faults should not follow a teacher. If you remember the old essays you are a new graduate. A man sitting at home may find disaster falling from the sky. Only ask that your heart be without shame, and do not fear later calamity. Only meet people with harmony; what quarrel ever kept the peace? The honest and generous have their honest reward; the violent and overbearing will surely suffer the punishment of officials. When a man enters the magistrate's gate, it is a good time to cultivate himself and to leave some hidden virtue for later. Why contend over high and low? When life is gone, all is over. The mountain is high, but not as high as the human heart, which is higher than Heaven. He turns water into wine to sell, and still grumbles that the pig has no lees. Do not complain in poverty; do not be proud in wealth and honour. Good and bad are done by people; fortune and misfortune are called down by themselves. I urge you, gentlemen, each to keep to yourself. If this alone is presented, ten thousand times there is no failure.

keyLines.line: 書中自有千鍾粟，書中自有顏如玉
keyLines.en: In books there is a thousand bushels of grain; in books there is a face like jade.
keyLines.note: Said to come from Emperor Zhenzong's 'Poem Urging Study' of the Song dynasty (960-1279); it uses fame and wealth to urge people to read.

keyLines.line: 別人騎馬我騎驢，仔細思量我不如，待我回頭看，還有挑腳漢
keyLines.en: Others ride horses and I ride a donkey; thinking it over I am worse off, but when I turn and look, there is still the porter carrying loads.
keyLines.note: Comparing downwards to teach contentment.

keyLines.line: 積錢積穀不如積德，買田買地不如買書
keyLines.en: To pile up money and grain is not as good as to pile up virtue; to buy fields and land is not as good as to buy books.
keyLines.note: Virtue and learning are worth more than money and land.

keyLines.line: 十分伶俐使七分，常留三分與兒孫
keyLines.en: Of ten parts of cleverness use seven, always leaving three for your sons and grandsons.
keyLines.note: Leave room in everything, and do not use up your own cleverness and fortune.

keyLines.line: 好學者則庶民之子為公卿，不好學者則公卿之子為庶民
keyLines.en: Those who love learning, even the child of a commoner may become a minister; those who do not, even the child of a minister may become a commoner.
keyLines.note: Learning can change one's station in society.

keyLines.line: 奉勸君子，各宜守己。只此呈示，萬無一失
keyLines.en: I urge you, gentlemen, each to keep to yourself. If this alone is presented, ten thousand times there is no failure.
keyLines.note: The closing words of the whole first part, urging people to keep to their station.

glossary.en: qian zhong su - 'a thousand zhong of grain'
glossary.note: A large salary. 「鍾」 was an ancient measure.

glossary.en: yan ru yu - 'a face like jade'
glossary.note: A jade-like face, meaning a beautiful woman.

glossary.en: tiao jiao han - 'a porter'
glossary.note: In old times, a carrier who bore baggage and goods for others.

glossary.en: chun gong - 'spring work'
glossary.note: The work of ploughing and sowing in spring.

glossary.en: ju zi - 'candidate'
glossary.note: A scholar sitting the imperial examinations.

glossary.en: yin de - 'hidden virtue'
glossary.note: Good done in secret.

glossary.en: wu xing ba zi - 'the five phases and the eight characters'
glossary.note: Telling a person's fate from the hour of birth: a popular system of fortune-telling.

pian16.background: This is the last section of the part collected here. The lines urging study are said to come from Emperor Zhenzong of the Northern Song (960-1127), though the attribution is disputed. The title Zengguang Xianwen means 'wise words added to and widened', and the lines come from many sources; the text has been added to and trimmed in copying.
